planting.note: Set out container-grown offsets after all frost danger has passed, planting high so the crown sits 1-2 inches above the soil line; in colder zones grow it in a pot that can be moved indoors for winter.

directions: This compact ornamental pineapple is grown mainly for its striped orange, red, and purple variegated foliage, with small red fruit forming as a seasonal bonus rather than the main attraction. Give it sharply drained soil and skip supplemental watering once established, since it is prone to rot in soggy conditions. It needs only a single early-spring feeding and no pruning, making it a low-fuss accent for patios, containers, or coastal landscapes.

scientific_name: Ilex integra x latifolia 'Screen Play' PP27524

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring, spacing them according to the eventual screen width desired; this hybrid holly builds a dense upright wall of foliage largely on its own.

directions: Screen Play is bred for fast, dense privacy screening, with large glossy spineless leaves tinged bronze when young and heavy crops of deep red winter berries on female plants. Give it well-drained soil and consistent moisture while it establishes a strong root system for its eventual height. Once mature it tolerates heat and drought well and rarely needs pruning beyond an annual shape-up, making it a low-maintenance substitute for older hedge hollies.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in a woodland border or shaded foundation bed; this upright mahonia fills vertical space without the sprawl of older species.

directions: Beijing Beauty brings year-round structure to shaded gardens with narrow, slightly spiny evergreen foliage and bright yellow flower spikes that open in late winter, followed by powdery blue-black berries. Plant it in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial sun to full shade, where it stays drought-tolerant once established and needs only an occasional cane removed at the base to maintain an upright shape. Its late-winter bloom and berries make it a reliable food source for early pollinators and birds.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring as a low hedge, edging, or boxwood substitute; its naturally rounded dwarf form needs little corrective shaping.

directions: Touch of Gold offers a warm alternative to green-leaved dwarf hollies and boxwoods, with small golden-variegated foliage held on a dense, mounding frame. Grow it in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade, where the gold color develops most strongly with more light exposure. It holds its tidy, rounded habit without regular pruning and can be lined out as a low hedge or used singly as a bright accent.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in a sunny foundation bed or mass planting; this disease-resistant selection was bred to replace older Indian hawthorns prone to leaf spot.

directions: Clean Sweep Snowbank forms a dense, mounding evergreen covered each spring in flower clusters that open blush pink and fade to crisp white, set against dark green leaves bred for strong resistance to the leaf spot that plagues older Indian hawthorns. Plant it in well-drained soil in full sun, where it tolerates salt spray and short dry spells without complaint. Its naturally full, compact form needs no routine pruning, just an annual early-spring feeding.

planting.note: Divide and plant offset rosettes in spring or fall in a rock garden, border edge, or container; this selection forms unusually large rosettes compared to typical hens-and-chicks.

directions: SUPERSEMPS Ruby produces plate-sized rosettes that deepen from green to dark burgundy-red as they mature, steadily ringed by new offset chicks. Plant it in sharply drained, gritty soil in full sun to part shade, where it needs almost no supplemental water beyond occasional rain. It is slower to bloom than many sempervivums, so expect years of expanding rosette color before any flower stalk appears, and simply remove spent rosettes after flowering to keep the clump tidy.

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in a border, rock garden, or container; this hybrid combines the upright flax-like form of one parent with the other's deep blue leaf color.

directions: Clarity Blue holds strongly upright, Phormium-like blades of true blue color through every season, keeping its form without the floppiness of older dianellas. Grow it in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade, where it tolerates heat, drought, and coastal salt exposure once established. It combines well with succulents in borders or containers and needs little more than an occasional trim of spent foliage to stay sharp-looking.
